later_events.mechanism: express revocation of Executive Order No. 9 (1873) and, by section 2, of orders amending it, including this order (the first end)

clauses.reason: The first clause amends “the Executive Order of January 17, 1873, as amended” to permit officers and employees of the Social Security Board, Federal Security Agency, “upon recommendation of the Board and approval of the Federal Security Administrator”, to hold office under state, territorial and municipal governments engaged in cooperative work with the Board. EO 11408 section 2 states that all prior orders “insofar as they interpret or amend Executive Order No. 9 are hereby revoked” and lists this order (number 8399) among them; section 1 revoked Executive Order No. 9 itself. This clause is wholly an exception to the revoked prohibition, so the revocation reaches all of it; it first ended on April 25, 1968 (signing date; no effective-date provision). First end: express revocation. The 1946 abolition of the Social Security Board is not held and is not relied on; see the order-level rationale.

The held text of EO 11408 decides: section 2 revokes all prior orders only insofar as they interpret or amend Executive Order No. 9, and every provision of EO 8399 is an amendment of Executive Order No. 9 (it is wholly two exceptions to the 1873 prohibition), so insofar as reaches all of EO 8399 and nothing of it remained in force; section 1 had already revoked Executive Order No. 9 itself, so no part of the order had anything left to operate on.

research_rationale:
EO 8399 (signed 1940-04-29; 5 FR 1607, filed 1940-04-30) was read in full in the held Federal Register text layer. Acting under section 1753 of the Revised Statutes, it further amends the Executive Order of January 17, 1873, as amended (Executive Order No. 9, the prohibition on federal officers and employees holding state, territorial and municipal office), so as (1) to permit officers and employees of the Social Security Board, Federal Security Agency, on the Board's recommendation and the Federal Security Administrator's approval, to hold state, territorial and municipal office in cooperative work with the Board, and (2) to permit state, territorial and municipal officers engaged in that work to accept appointment under the Board, with civil-service appointments made under the civil-service laws. The two permissions are two clauses (the lead is folded into the first). The order states no expiry, condition or temporary term. EO 11408 (signed 1968-04-25) section 1 revoked Executive Order No. 9 of 1873 itself and section 2 revoked all prior orders insofar as they interpret or amend it, naming this order in its list of amendatory orders; because this order is wholly an amendment of the revoked order, both clauses first ended on 1968-04-25 by express revocation, which is also the whole-order end (the held text has no effective-date provision; the signing date is used). Open point disclosed for the reviewer: the Social Security Board named in both clauses was abolished by Reorganization Plan No. 2 of 1946, which is not held; no held source shows that the plan, or any other instrument, extinguished or ended these permissions before 1968, so the express revocation is the first documented end, and whether the permissions had already become inoperable in 1946 is not established. Original not an authenticated transcription: the held text is the OCR text layer of the official Federal Register issue; quotations avoid its recognition errors.

savings.reason: EO 11408 contains no savings, transition or continuation clause. Its section 1 revoked the prohibition itself and its section 2 revoked the amendatory orders, so nothing remained for these exceptions to operate on; office-holding done under the permissions before 1968 was lawful when done and creates no continuing right or duty.
